messages:
sylvia: Quick sync — noticed a persistent drop in prefix-cache hit rate on shard-A after long runs (~6h). Metric went from ~0.42 -> 0.27 while QPS stayed flat. My hunch: TTLs aren't being refreshed on shard handoff/rehash and prefixes get treated as cold. Can someone run a small profiling + a bench to reproduce?

sylvia: Things I'd like: 1) perf trace + flame for node-12 during a repro window 2) tail of kc_stats on shard-A for last 500 lines 3) a short bench run to exercise prefix locality (10m) — see recommended cmd below.

sylvia: bench command (dev cluster):
```
ssh perf@kv-perf-1 \
  'tools/bench/kv_hit_perf.py --duration 10m --clients 8 --prefix-dist heavy_tail --shard shard-A --out s3://redwood-kv-dumps/sylvia/185912/'
```

sylvia: kc_stats tail: `kc_stats --shard=shard-A --tail 500`

maria: I'll kick off the bench on kv-perf in ~5m and upload logs to s3. tagging @tony for perf. ETA ~12m. :+1:

tony: OK I'll grab `perf record` + `perf script` on node-12 during the run. Use events: `-e cpu-clock -e cycles` and `-g` for stacks. Command I'll run:
```
perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 600
perf script > /tmp/perf-node12-185912.out
```

alex: Quick check — also inspect metrics `metrics.kv.prefix_evictions` and `metrics.kv.prefix_ttl_reset_count`. If ttl_reset_count is near zero while evictions climb, that matches the leak theory. I'll add a short dashboard check.

bench-bot: benchmark started on kv-perf-1 (run id: bb-185912-01). Posting progress logs to s3://redwood-kv-dumps/sylvia/185912/ .

infra-bot: reminder: please run this on the kv-perf namespace and not on prod. If you need more capacity, ping infra.

maria: bench finished. Uploads complete. Link: s3://redwood-kv-dumps/sylvia/185912/run-logs.tar.gz

maria: quick numbers from the run (aggregate, 10m window): prefix_hit_rate: 0.29, prefix_evictions (shard-A): 11.3/min, ttl_reset_count: 2 total.

tony: perf sample attached to same bucket: s3://redwood-kv-dumps/sylvia/185912/perf-node12-185912.out.gz. Early glance: ~40% of samples in `kv/handle_prefix` path, with a hot call in `refresh_prefix_metadata` that looks suspicious (lots of memcmp).

alex: Dashboard shows ttl_reset_count ~0. Low. Also saw a small spike in `prefix_rehashes` at the 4.5h mark which corresponds with your handoff windows.

sylvia: Thanks — that aligns. Action items: (A) maria/tony: reproduce with `--prefix-dist skewed_hot` and capture perf + kc_stats; (B) I will open an instrumentation change to increment `prefix_ttl_reset_count` at more code locations and add a guard in `refresh_prefix_metadata`; (C) alex will watch the A/B shard rollout for any correlation.

maria: Running the skewed_hot run now (10m). Will post results to same s3 path.

bench-bot: benchmark started (bb-185912-02) with prefix-dist=skewed_hot.

maria: results: prefix_hit_rate: 0.56, prefix_evictions: 2.1/min, ttl_reset_count: 18. So hot-skew shows expected behavior.

sylvia: Great signal. I'll push a small PR with extra TTL resets + a unit test that simulates handoff. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-runtime/pull/4123 — please review when you have a moment.

tony: I'll review perf traces against the new branch once PR is up. If we see memcmp hotpath reduced after the guard, that's a win.

alex: I'll add alerting: fire if prefix_evictions > 5/min AND ttl_reset_count < 5 over 15m.

sylvia: Thanks team. If anyone finds divergence in other shards, drop notes here. I'll follow up with a short postmortem-ish note with links to runs and perf traces. :white_check_mark:
